question.text: Which of the following is an Officially Valid Document (OVD) under PML Rules for Proof of Identity?

answer.text: All of these -- Passport, Driving Licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter's ID, NREGA Job Card, NPR Letter
Only Voter's ID and Driving Licence

explanation.text: The Logic: OVDs under Rule 2(d) of the PML Rules include: (i) passport, (ii) driving licence, (iii) proof of possession of Aadhaar number, (iv) Voter's ID issued by the Election Commission of India, (v) NREGA job card duly signed by an officer of the State Government, (vi) NPR letter containing name and address, and (vii) any other document notified by the Central Government. The Trap: PAN card is mandatory for many securities-market transactions but is not itself an OVD under the PML Rules. "Only Passport and Aadhaar" and "Only Voter's ID and Driving Licence" each list only a subset of the statutory OVDs. Note: Option A reworded to mirror the statutory phrase "proof of possession of Aadhaar number" rather than "Aadhaar" alone; distributor-style pro-tip and cross-exam framing removed.
